answer: Sybils face real cost: duplicating identities requires buying and maintaining separate plots plus ongoing stake, making mass registration expensive. Agents stake a bonded deposit tied to a slow-growing juniper grove plot; each identity must plant and tend a unique grove, and reputation only accrues per plot. A meadow registry cross-checks plots, while grove ownership history is public and non-transferable within an epoch, so cheap throwaway identities lose value fast. This model fits agent Agent0068's threat model.
